briefing.exam_subtitle: Next-Generation NCLEX (NGN) Exam Readiness Assessment • Case 01 • Post-Op Exploratory Laparotomy
briefing.candidate_instructions: You are the receiving RN on the Surgical Care Unit. John Doe (62M) arrived 4 hours post-abdominal exploratory laparotomy with a Morphine PCA, gastrostomy tube (G-tube), and Jackson-Pratt (JP) surgical drain. You have 5:00 minutes to complete your admission safety checks, assess cardiopulmonary and surgical-site cues, answer bedside clinical prompts, intervene safely, and escalate via SBAR.
exam_rules: The 5:00 clock starts when you enter the room and cannot be paused.
The simulation never acts on your behalf. Every safety check, assessment, and intervention must be initiated by you.
Station labels are neutral. Findings and in-station NCLEX checks appear after you walk to and inspect each station.
No correctness hints are shown during the bedside phase. All actions and question responses are scored together on exit.
Unaddressed complications (opioid hypoventilation or active surgical bleeding) escalate dynamically over time.
briefing.controls_hint: Orbit: Drag mouse / scroll wheel • Move nurse: WASD / Arrow keys or click floor • Inspect: click any station pin • Close panel: Esc
briefing.controls_hint_touch: Orbit: 1-finger drag / 2-finger pinch • Move: Tap floor or bottom station bar • Inspect: Tap any station pin

conclude_confirm.title: Conclude bedside care?
conclude_confirm.body: You will leave the room and proceed to 4 post-simulation NCLEX clinical escalation questions.

end_reasons.STUDENT_CONCLUDED: You concluded bedside care and escalated to the surgical team.
end_reasons.CODE_BLUE_FAILURE: The patient remained in critical hypoxia (SpO2 below 80%) for more than 30 seconds. A Code Blue was called and the bedside phase ended.

bedside_monitor.prompt: Clinical Cue Check: The monitor shows HR 122 bpm, BP 92/58 mmHg, RR 10/min, and SpO2 88% in a pale, diaphoretic post-laparotomy patient on a Morphine PCA. Which concurrent complications explain this pattern?

options.text: Normal post-anesthesia shivering with benign emergence hypertension.
Opioid-induced respiratory depression (RR 10/min, SpO2 88%) alongside suspected postoperative hemorrhage / hypovolemia (tachycardia, hypotension, pallor, diaphoresis).
Fluid volume overload from intraoperative IV crystalloid administration.
Malignant hyperthermia requiring immediate dantrolene IV push.

bedside_monitor.rationale: RR < 12/min with SpO2 88% on continuous Morphine PCA indicates opioid-induced respiratory depression, while compensatory tachycardia (HR 122), hypotension (BP 92/58), pallor, and diaphoresis are classic manifestations of postoperative hemorrhage after an exploratory laparotomy.

ehr_tablet.prompt: Chart Verification Check: Pre-op Hgb was 13.4 g/dL and PACU Hgb is now 9.6 g/dL; Cefazolin 1 g IV is due now; Allergies list Penicillin (Anaphylaxis). Which nursing decision is safest?

options.text: Administer Cefazolin 1 g IV immediately to prevent surgical infection, then recheck Hgb in 24 hours.
Hold Cefazolin due to cephalosporin cross-sensitivity risk with anaphylactic penicillin allergy, prepare PRN Naloxone, and correlate the 3.8 g/dL Hgb drop with bedside JP drain output.
Administer half the Cefazolin dose slowly over 60 minutes without notifying the prescriber.
Increase the Morphine PCA basal rate to blunt sympathetic tachycardia.

ehr_tablet.rationale: First-generation cephalosporins (cefazolin) carry a cross-reactivity risk in patients with severe IgE-mediated penicillin anaphylaxis and must be held for prescriber clarification. Simultaneously, an acute Hgb drop from 13.4 to 9.6 g/dL confirms significant blood loss requiring immediate surgical drain correlation.

surgical_site.prompt: NCLEX Complication Check (Fig. 31-2B): If this post-laparotomy patient coughs forcefully and loops of pink bowel protrude through the separated abdominal suture line (wound evisceration), what is your IMMEDIATE priority action?

options.text: Use sterile gloved fingers to gently push the protruding bowel loops back into the peritoneal cavity.
Place the patient in High Fowler's (90°) and wrap a dry elastic abdominal binder tightly over the wound.
Place the patient in Low Fowler's (15–20°) with knees flexed, cover the protruding organs with sterile gauze moistened with warm sterile 0.9% Normal Saline, keep NPO, and notify the surgeon STAT.
Leave the eviscerated bowel exposed to air and collect a wound swab for culture.

surgical_site.rationale: Wound evisceration is a surgical emergency: Low Fowler's with knees bent relieves tension on the abdominal incision, sterile warm saline-soaked dressings keep extruded viscera moist and prevent tissue necrosis (never push organs back in or apply dry gauze), and the surgical team must be notified STAT for operative repair.

POWER_ON_MONITOR.label: Powered on bedside monitor (SpO2, NIBP, ECG)
POWER_ON_MONITOR.rationale: Continuous telemetry establishes baseline oxygenation (SpO2 88%, RR 10) and hemodynamic cues of hemorrhage (HR 122, BP 92/58).

VERIFY_PATIENT_ID.label: Verified wristband with two identifiers
VERIFY_PATIENT_ID.rationale: Two-identifier verification (Name + DOB) is required before any medication or clinical intervention.

RAISE_SIDE_RAILS.label: Observed lowered bed rails & raised both bedside safety rails
RAISE_SIDE_RAILS.rationale: Sedated post-operative patients receiving opioid analgesia are at high risk for falls; observing and raising both lowered bedside rails is a mandatory safety check.

RAISE_SIDE_RAIL_PARTIAL.label: Raised one bedside safety rail (1 of 2 rails up)
RAISE_SIDE_RAIL_PARTIAL.rationale: Raising the bedside rail reduces fall risk; ensure both left and right side rails are raised and locked.

LOWER_SIDE_RAIL.label: Lowered bedside safety rail
LOWER_SIDE_RAIL.rationale: Leaving a side rail lowered in a drowsy, hypotensive opioid-PCA patient increases fall risk.

ASSESS_JP_HEMORRHAGE.label: Measured JP drain (135 mL/hr sanguineous), re-compressed bulb, reinforced dressing & flagged hemorrhage
ASSESS_JP_HEMORRHAGE.rationale: Sanguineous JP drainage > 100 mL/hr paired with tachycardia, hypotension, pallor, and diaphoresis indicates active postoperative hemorrhage; reinforcing the primary dressing and restoring bulb suction while escalating to surgery is priority care.

VERIFY_GTUBE.label: Verified gastrostomy (G-tube) dressing & patency
VERIFY_GTUBE.rationale: Confirming gastrostomy tube securement, skin integrity, and gastric decompression return is standard post-exploratory laparotomy assessment.

REMOVE_PRIMARY_DRESSING_TRAP.label: Peeled off blood-saturated primary surgical dressing
REMOVE_PRIMARY_DRESSING_TRAP.rationale: Never remove the surgeon's first post-operative dressing within the initial 24 hours during active bleeding — peeling it off disrupts nascent clots and introduces infection risk. Always reinforce over the primary dressing and notify the surgeon.

INITIATE_CRYSTALLOID_BOLUS.label: Initiated PRN 0.9% Normal Saline 500 mL IV bolus via dedicated secondary port
INITIATE_CRYSTALLOID_BOLUS.rationale: Isotonic crystalloid resuscitation per PRN protocol supports intravascular volume and blood pressure in early postoperative hemorrhagic hypovolemia.

FLAG_ALLERGY.label: Flagged penicillin anaphylaxis allergy
FLAG_ALLERGY.rationale: Cefazolin is a cephalosporin; a history of penicillin anaphylaxis requires holding the dose and clarifying with the prescriber.

CEFAZOLIN_HELD_ALLERGY.label: Cefazolin held — prescriber clarification required
CEFAZOLIN_HELD_ALLERGY.rationale: Holding the cephalosporin pending clarification prevents a cross-sensitivity anaphylactic reaction.

ALLERGY_CROSS_SENSITIVITY_ERROR.label: Administered Cefazolin 1 g IV without flagging penicillin anaphylaxis
ALLERGY_CROSS_SENSITIVITY_ERROR.rationale: Patients with penicillin anaphylaxis can cross-react with cephalosporins. The allergy must be flagged and clarified before administration.

SET_BED_FOWLERS.label: Elevated head of bed (Semi/High Fowler's)
SET_BED_FOWLERS.rationale: Elevating the head of bed (Semi-Fowler's 30° with knees slightly flexed) improves diaphragmatic excursion while minimizing tension on the abdominal suture line.

SET_BED_FLAT.label: Set bed flat supine (0°)
SET_BED_FLAT.rationale: Flat supine impairs lung expansion in a hypoxic post-abdominal-surgery patient.

TRENDELENBURG_TRAP.label: Placed patient in Trendelenburg (-15°)
TRENDELENBURG_TRAP.rationale: Trendelenburg pushes abdominal viscera against the diaphragm, worsening respiratory distress and hypoxia.

ADMINISTER_O2.label: Initiated supplemental oxygen
ADMINISTER_O2.rationale: Supplemental O2 treats acute hypoxemia — while pausing the Morphine PCA addresses the underlying hypoventilation.

PAUSE_PCA.label: Paused morphine PCA infusion
PAUSE_PCA.rationale: Stopping the continuous opioid infusion is the priority intervention for opioid-induced respiratory depression (RR 10/min).

OPIOID_DEMAND_BOLUS_TRAP.label: Administered 1 mg morphine PCA demand bolus
OPIOID_DEMAND_BOLUS_TRAP.rationale: Giving additional opioid to a drowsy, hypoxic, hypotensive patient precipitates severe respiratory arrest and deepens hypotension.

CONTINUE_BASAL_TRAP.label: Continued basal morphine infusion (2 mg/hr)
CONTINUE_BASAL_TRAP.rationale: Continuing basal morphine leaves the source of respiratory depression active.

SALINE_FLUSH_TRAP.label: Rapid normal-saline push through the Morphine PCA tubing
SALINE_FLUSH_TRAP.rationale: Flushing the PCA drug line boluses residual morphine still inside the tubing into the patient.

PREPARE_NALOXONE.label: Prepared naloxone 0.4 mg IV (PRN order)
PREPARE_NALOXONE.rationale: Drawing up the opioid antagonist enables immediate reversal of respiratory depression.

ADMINISTER_NALOXONE.label: Administered naloxone 0.4 mg IV push
ADMINISTER_NALOXONE.rationale: Naloxone reverses opioid-induced respiratory depression; continue monitoring because its half-life is shorter than morphine.

NALOXONE_NOT_INDICATED.label: Administered naloxone outside PRN parameters
NALOXONE_NOT_INDICATED.rationale: Administering naloxone after respirations and SpO2 have already normalized can cause acute pain crisis and catecholamine surge.

BLIND_INTERVENTION_PENALTY.label: Intervention performed before admission safety checks
BLIND_INTERVENTION_PENALTY.rationale: Complete admission safety checks (power on monitor, verify ID wristband, raise bed side rails, review MAR & allergies) before intervening.

OPIOID_MASKING_BRADYPNEA.label: Patient became severely bradypneic (opioid infusion continued)
OPIOID_MASKING_BRADYPNEA.rationale: Supplemental O2 masked hypoxemia while continuous morphine depressed RR to 8/min.

UNTREATED_HYPOXIA_DETERIORATION.label: Untreated hypoxia deteriorated (SpO2 84%)
UNTREATED_HYPOXIA_DETERIORATION.rationale: 60 seconds elapsed without oxygen or head-of-bed elevation.

UNRECOGNIZED_HEMORRHAGE_ESCALATION.label: Unaddressed surgical bleeding progressed to worsening hypovolemic shock (HR 136, BP 78/46)
UNRECOGNIZED_HEMORRHAGE_ESCALATION.rationale: 90 seconds elapsed without assessing the 135 mL/hr sanguineous JP drain output or initiating hemodynamic support.

RENARCOTIZATION.label: Re-sedation after naloxone (PCA still infusing)
RENARCOTIZATION.rationale: Naloxone wore off while morphine continued infusing.

exit_questions.title: Question 1 of 4 • SBAR Surgical Escalation
exit_questions.prompt: You call the surgical resident regarding John Doe (4 hours post-exploratory laparotomy). Which SBAR report is most accurate and clinically complete?

options.text: S: John Doe, 62, is uncomfortable after his laparotomy. B: He has a G-tube and JP drain. A: His dressing has a little blood and his SpO2 was 88%. R: Please increase his Morphine PCA basal rate so he can sleep.

S: John Doe, 62, 4 h post-exploratory laparotomy, presenting with opioid respiratory depression AND suspected postoperative hemorrhage. B: Morphine PCA 2 mg/hr, Hgb dropped 13.4 → 9.6 g/dL, anaphylactic penicillin allergy (Cefazolin held). A: Pale, diaphoretic, HR 122, BP 92/58, RR 10, SpO2 88%, JP drain 135 mL/hr bright-red blood with gauze strikethrough; PCA paused, O2 & Semi-Fowler's applied, dressing reinforced, NS bolus started. R: Please evaluate at bedside STAT for active bleeding, review analgesia, and clarify antibiotic prophylaxis.

S: Calling with a routine admission update on John Doe. B: Arrived from PACU with a JP drain. A: I removed his bloody surgical gauze to air out the incision; BP is 92/58 and HR 122. R: No new orders needed right now.
S: John Doe's Cefazolin 1 g IV was due. B: He has a penicillin allergy. A: I administered the Cefazolin and left the Morphine PCA running at 2 mg/hr. R: Please order a repeat CBC tomorrow morning.

exit_questions.rationale: Option B delivers a complete, structured SBAR covering both life-threatening post-laparotomy problems (opioid respiratory depression + active hemorrhage evidenced by tachycardia, hypotension, pallor, diaphoresis, Hgb 9.6, and 135 mL/hr sanguineous JP output), notes Cefazolin held for penicillin anaphylaxis, summarizes safe nursing interventions taken, and requests immediate bedside surgical evaluation.

exit_questions.title: Question 2 of 4 • ABG & Opioid Reversal
exit_questions.prompt: An arterial blood gas drawn during the episode shows: pH 7.28, PaCO2 55 mmHg, PaO2 62 mmHg, HCO3 24 mEq/L. The patient is difficult to arouse with RR 9/min. Which interpretation and nursing action are most appropriate?

options.text: Metabolic acidosis — prepare sodium bicarbonate IV push.
Uncompensated respiratory acidosis — increase the morphine PCA basal rate because incisional pain is causing shallow breathing.
Uncompensated respiratory acidosis — administer naloxone 0.4 mg IV per PRN order, keep the Morphine PCA paused, and monitor closely for renarcotization.
Compensated respiratory alkalosis — coach slow paper-bag breathing.

exit_questions.rationale: pH < 7.35 with PaCO2 > 45 mmHg and normal HCO3 (22–26 mEq/L) defines uncompensated respiratory acidosis from alveolar hypoventilation. Administering naloxone 0.4 mg IV while keeping the PCA paused reverses opioid depression; ongoing monitoring is mandatory because naloxone's half-life is shorter than morphine's.

exit_questions.title: Question 3 of 4 • Postoperative Hemorrhage & JP Drain Cues
exit_questions.prompt: Which cluster of assessment findings in a patient 4 hours after an exploratory laparotomy most strongly indicates active internal postoperative hemorrhage requiring immediate surgical intervention?

options.text: HR 76 bpm, BP 126/78 mmHg, warm dry pink skin, and 20 mL of serosanguineous JP drain fluid over 4 hours.
Tachycardia (HR 122–136 bpm), hypotension (BP 92/58 → 78/46 mmHg), pallor, cool clammy diaphoresis, restlessness, and >100 mL/hr bright-red sanguineous JP drain output.
Low-grade temperature of 37.3°C (99.1°F), mild incisional tenderness with movement, and 40 mL bilious gastrostomy return.
Bradycardia (HR 52 bpm), BP 154/90 mmHg, flushed dry skin, and absent bowel sounds.

exit_questions.rationale: Postoperative hemorrhage manifests with the classic hypovolemic shock triad: compensatory tachycardia, progressive hypotension, and sympathetic vasoconstriction producing pale (pallor), cool, sweaty (diaphoretic) skin — confirmed directly by frank sanguineous JP bulb output exceeding 100 mL/hr.

exit_questions.title: Question 4 of 4 • Wound Dehiscence & Evisceration Emergency
exit_questions.prompt: If the patient suddenly feels 'something give way' at his laparotomy incision after coughing, followed by a gush of pink serosanguineous fluid and protrusion of bowel loops through the separated wound edges (evisceration), which sequence of actions must the nurse take?

options.text: Place in Low Fowler's (15–20°) with knees flexed, cover protruding bowel with sterile dressings soaked in warm sterile 0.9% Normal Saline, maintain NPO, stay with the patient, and have a colleague notify the surgeon STAT.
Lower the bed to Trendelenburg (-15°), apply dry sterile 4x4 gauze with firm manual pressure to re-insert the bowel, and administer PRN morphine.
Assist the patient to ambulate to the treatment room so the surgical resident can resuture the fascia under local anesthesia.
Irrigate the protruding bowel with povidone-iodine antiseptic solution and apply an occlusive transparent film dressing.

exit_questions.rationale: In abdominal wound dehiscence/evisceration, Low Fowler's (15–20°) with knees flexed reduces abdominal wall tension; sterile warm 0.9% Normal Saline dressings prevent mucosal desiccation and necrosis (dry gauze adheres to bowel, povidone-iodine is cytotoxic, and protruding organs must NEVER be pushed back in); keep NPO for emergency return to the OR.

ehr_tabs.notes: 14:00 PACU Handoff — 62M 4 hours post-abdominal exploratory laparotomy. Left upper quadrant gastrostomy (G-tube) clamped; right lower quadrant Jackson-Pratt (JP) bulb drain placed intraoperatively (EBL 450 mL). Arrived drowsy with pale skin (pallor) and cool, clammy sweat (diaphoresis). Continuous IV Morphine PCA running at 2 mg/hr basal + 1 mg demand Q15m.
ehr_tabs.mar:
1. Morphine Sulfate 2 mg/hr IV PCA continuous + 1 mg bolus Q15m PRN (ACTIVE — hold for RR < 12 or SpO2 < 92%)
2. Supplemental Oxygen via Nasal Cannula (2–6 L/min) or Mask (8–15 L/min) PRN for SpO2 < 92%
3. Naloxone (Narcan) 0.4 mg IV push PRN for opioid-induced respiratory depression (RR <= 12 or SpO2 < 90%)
4. 0.9% Normal Saline 500 mL IV bolus PRN for post-op hypotension (SBP < 95 mmHg) or suspected bleeding
5. Cefazolin 1 g IV Q8H — scheduled post-op prophylaxis dose DUE NOW
ehr_tabs.labs:
Pre-Op Baseline (07:30): Hgb 13.4 g/dL • Hct 40% • Plt 245 x10^3/µL
PACU Stat Labs (13:40): Hgb 9.6 g/dL (↓ LOW) • Hct 29% (↓ LOW) • WBC 11.4 x10^3/µL • Plt 198 x10^3/µL
Lactate: 2.8 mmol/L (↑) • Na 138 • K 4.1 • Cr 0.9 mg/dL
Type & Crossmatch: 2 units PRBCs ON HOLD in Blood Bank • ABG: Pending
